hindi: अब इसके बाद हम यज्जःपुरुषीय अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter Yajjaḥpuruṣīya ('born of what is the person').
notes: Prose opening formula of the chapter; the unit is typed as a verse in the input but is a prose line. The chapter name takes up the question of unit 6 (puruṣo yajjaḥ).

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा।
english: Thus said the venerable Ātreya.

hindi: प्राचीन काल में, धर्म का प्रत्यक्ष दर्शन करने वाले जो महर्षि भगवान् पुनर्वसु के पास एकत्र हुए थे, उनके बीच यह चर्चा उठी—
english: Long ago, among the great sages who had perceived dharma directly and had assembled around the venerable Punarvasu, this discussion arose

text_flags.why: the name is printed punarvasuḥ in units 6 and 26 of this chunk; punaravasum gives 9 syllables in the pāda, punarvasum the required 8

notes: The sentence continues in unit 4. sametānām with the accusative bhagavantam: 'gathered around (him)'. The genitives are rendered 'among'.

words.gloss: of self, senses, mind and objects

hindi: —आत्मा, इन्द्रियों, मन और अर्थों का यह जो पुरुष नामक राशि है, उसकी और उसके रोगों की पूर्व उत्पत्ति के निर्णय के विषय में।
english: concerning the determination of the prior origin of this aggregate of self, senses, mind and sense-objects which is called the person (puruṣa), and of its diseases.

text_flags.why: vinścaye is not a word; viniścaye 'in determining' fits the sense, and the pāda then has 8 syllables instead of 7

notes: Continues the sentence of unit 3. manorthānām = mano'rthānām (avagraha not printed). The relative clause (yo 'yaṃ ... rāśiḥ) stands for the genitive 'of this aggregate'.

hindi: तब काशी के स्वामी, अर्थ के ज्ञाता वामक ने ऋषियों की सभा के पास जाकर और अभिवादन करके यह वचन कहा—
english: Thereupon Vāmaka, lord of Kāśi, a knower of meaning, having approached the assembly of sages and saluted it, uttered these words:
notes: tadantaram taken as an adverb, 'thereupon' (literally 'in that interval').

hindi: 'हे सज्जनो, क्या पुरुष जिससे उत्पन्न होता है, उसके रोग उससे उत्पन्न माने गए हैं, या नहीं?' राजा के ऐसा कहने पर पुनर्वसु ने ऋषियों से कहा—
english: 'Sirs, are the diseases of the person held to be born of that of which the person is born, or not?' When the king had said this, Punarvasu spoke to the sages:
notes: ukte narendreṇa is a locative absolute.

words.gloss: whose doubts are cut by boundless knowledge and specialised knowledge

hindi: आप सब, जिनके संशय असीम ज्ञान और विज्ञान से कट चुके हैं, काशिराज के संशय को काटने में समर्थ हैं।
english: All of you, whose doubts have been cut away by boundless knowledge and specialised knowledge (vijñāna), are able to cut away the doubt of the king of Kāśi.

text_flags.why: visarga of bhavantaḥ before ch becomes ś (grammar); printed -ac- is not a possible sandhi

notes: sarva evā- = sarve eva (e before a vowel becomes a). bhavantac-chettum = bhavantaḥ chettum. Spoken by Punarvasu (unit 6).

hindi: पारीक्षि मौद्गल्य ने उस पर पहले विचार करके यह वचन कहा— 'पुरुष आत्मा से उत्पन्न है और रोग आत्मा से उत्पन्न हैं, क्योंकि वह (आत्मा) कारण है।'
english: Pārīkṣi Maudgalya, having first examined it, spoke these words: 'The person is born of the self (ātman), and the diseases are born of the self; for it is the cause.'
notes: Pārīkṣi Maudgalya taken as one person (name and patronymic) because of the singular verb abravīt.
lines_deva: आत्मजः पुरुषो रोगाश्चात्मजाः कारणं हि सः

hindi: वह कर्म का संचय करता है और कर्मफलों का भोग करता है; क्योंकि चेतना-धातु के बिना सुख और दुःख की प्रवृत्ति नहीं होती।
english: It accumulates action (karma) and experiences the fruits of action; for without the conscious element (cetanādhātu) there is no occurrence of pleasure and pain.
notes: Continues Maudgalya's view. The two verbs and two objects are taken pairwise (accumulates action, experiences its fruits).
lines_deva: स चिनोत्युपभुङ्क्ते च कर्म कर्मफलानि च

hindi: परन्तु शरलोमा ने कहा— 'नहीं; क्योंकि दुःख से द्वेष करने वाला आत्मा स्वयं अपने को दुःखरूप व्याधियों से कभी नहीं जोड़ेगा।'
english: But Śaraloman said 'No': for the self, which hates sorrow, would never by itself join itself with diseases, which are sorrows.
notes: duḥkhaiḥ is taken in apposition to vyādhibhiḥ ('with diseases, [that is,] sorrows').

hindi: किन्तु रजस् और तमस् से व्याप्त, सत्त्व नामक मन शरीर की और विकारों की उत्पत्ति में कारण है।
english: Rather, the mind, called sattva, pervaded by rajas and tamas, is the cause in the origin of the body and of disorders.
notes: Continues Śaraloman's view (unit 10). The locative samutpattau is taken with both genitives (śarīrasya, vikārāṇām).

hindi: वार्योविद ने कहा— 'नहीं; क्योंकि अकेला मन कारण नहीं है। शरीर के बिना न शारीरिक रोग होते हैं, न मन की स्थिति होती है।'
english: But Vāryovida said 'No': for the mind alone is not the cause; without the body there are no bodily diseases, nor any abiding of the mind.
lines_deva: वार्योविदस्तु नेत्याह न ह्येकं कारणं मनः
lines_iast: vāryovidastu netyāha na hyekaṃ kāraṇaṃ manaḥ

hindi: किन्तु प्राणी और नाना प्रकार की व्याधियाँ रस से उत्पन्न होते हैं; क्योंकि रस वाले वे जल उत्पत्ति के कारण माने गए हैं।
english: Rather, beings are born of rasa, and so are diseases of various kinds; for the waters, those possessing rasa, are held to be the causes of their coming into being.

text_flags.why: the printed form has a stray i after ṛ (Devanagari निर्वृइत्ति), which is not a possible spelling; nirvṛtti 'coming into being' fits the sense, and the pāda then has 8 syllables instead of 9

notes: Continues Vāryovida's view (unit 12). rasa is left as rasa; the line does not decide between 'fluid' and 'taste'.

words.gloss: born of sound and the rest

hindi: हिरण्याक्ष ने कहा— 'नहीं; क्योंकि आत्मा रस से उत्पन्न नहीं माना गया है, न इन्द्रियों से परे मन; और इसी प्रकार शब्द आदि से उत्पन्न रोग होते हैं।'
english: But Hiraṇyākṣa said 'No': for the self is not held to be born of rasa, nor is the mind, which is beyond the senses; and likewise there are diseases born of sound and the rest.
lines_deva: हिरण्याक्षस्तु नेत्याह न ह्यात्मा रसजः स्मृतः
lines_iast: hiraṇyākṣastu netyāha na hyātmā rasajaḥ smṛtaḥ

hindi: किन्तु पुरुष छह धातुओं से उत्पन्न है, तथा रोग छह धातुओं से उत्पन्न हैं; क्योंकि प्राचीन सांख्यों ने इस राशि को छह धातुओं से उत्पन्न बताया है।
english: Rather, the person is born of six dhātus, and the diseases likewise are born of six dhātus; for this aggregate has been proclaimed by the early Sāṃkhyas to be born of six dhātus.

text_flags.why: before the voiced dh the ṭ of ṣaṭ becomes ḍ; line 2 of the same unit prints ṣaḍdhātujo
same sandhi error as ṣaṭdhātujastu; line 2 of the unit prints ṣaḍdhātujo

notes: The speaker is not named in this unit; unit 16 calls the one speaking thus Kuśika. The six dhātus are not listed in the unit.

words.gram: m. acc. sg., pres. part. mid. √brū

hindi: ऐसा कहते हुए कुशिक से कौषिक ने कहा— 'वह ठीक नहीं; माता-पिता के बिना छह धातुओं से उत्पन्न (पुरुष) भला कैसे होगा?'
english: To Kuśika, speaking thus, Kauṣika said 'That is not so: how indeed could one born of six dhātus come into being without mother and father?'

text_flags.why: kasamān is not a form; kasmāt (kasmān before m) 'how, why' fits the question, and the pāda then has 8 syllables instead of 9

notes: kuśikam names the speaker of the view in unit 15. hi here is taken as emphatic in a question. Name kept as printed (kauṣikaḥ); the same line names the other speaker Kuśika (kuśikam).

hindi: मनुष्य से मनुष्य, गाय से गाय और घोड़े से घोड़ा उत्पन्न होता है; और मेह आदि रोग पैतृक कहे गए हैं; यहाँ वे दोनों (माता-पिता) कारण हैं।
english: Man is born from man, a cow from a cow, a horse from a horse; and diseases such as meha are spoken of as hereditary; those two (mother and father) are the cause here.
notes: Continues Kauṣika's view (unit 16). pitrya, literally 'coming from the fathers (ancestors)'. tau refers to the mother and father of unit 16. gauḥ may be m. or f.; taken as 'cow'.

hindi: भद्रकाप्य ने कहा— 'नहीं; क्योंकि अन्धे से अन्धा उत्पन्न नहीं होता; और तुम्हारे मत में माता-पिता में भी पूर्व उत्पत्ति युक्तिसंगत नहीं है।'
english: But Bhadrakāpya said 'No': for a blind man is not born from a blind man; and, for you, a prior origin in the mother and father too is not tenable.
notes: te is taken as the enclitic of tvam ('for you', addressed to Kauśika); a reading as m. nom. pl. 'they' finds no plural predicate in the line. mātāpitroḥ may be genitive or locative dual. The exact point of line 2 is not fully clear from the wording.

hindi: किन्तु प्राणी कर्म से उत्पन्न माना गया है और उसके रोग कर्म से उत्पन्न हैं; क्योंकि कर्म के बिना न रोगों का जन्म होता है, न पुरुष का।
english: Rather, the person is held to be born of action (karma), and his diseases are born of action; for without action there is no birth of diseases or of the person.

text_flags.why: the y of hi is missing: unit 9 of this chunk prints the same phrase as nahyṛte (na hi ṛte); nahṛte gives no sense

notes: Continues Bhadrakāpya's view (unit 18).

lines_iast: nahṛte karmaṇo janma rogāṇāṃ puruṣasya vā

words.gram: n. nom. sg., ppp. √kṛ with neg. a-

hindi: भरद्वाज ने कहा— 'नहीं; क्योंकि कर्ता कर्म से पहले होता है; और बिना किया हुआ कोई कर्म नहीं देखा गया, जिसका फल पुरुष हो।'
english: But Bharadvāja said 'No': for the doer comes before the action; and no action that has not been done is seen, of which the person could be the fruit.

दृष्तं न चाकृतं कर्म यस्य स्यात् पुरुषः फलम्

dṛṣtaṃ na cākṛtaṃ karma yasya syāt puruṣaḥ phalam

hindi: किन्तु व्याधियों और पुरुष की सत्ता का कारण स्वभाव है, ठीक वैसे ही जैसे तेज-पर्यन्तों का खरत्व, द्रवत्व, चलत्व और उष्णत्व।
english: Rather, own nature (svabhāva) is the cause of the existence of diseases and of the person, just as roughness, fluidity, mobility and heat are of those ending with fire (tejas).
notes: Continues Bharadvāja's view (unit 20). tejontānām = tejo'ntānām (avagraha not printed). The four qualities are set against a series 'ending with tejas' whose members the line does not name.

hindi: काङ्कायन ने कहा— 'नहीं; क्योंकि (तब) आरम्भ का फल नहीं होगा; पदार्थों की असिद्धि और सिद्धि स्वभाव से ही होगी।'
english: But Kāṅkāyana said 'No': for (then) there would be no fruit of undertaking; the failure and the success of things would come just from their own nature.

text_flags.why: possible: cā is not a word; ca 'and' needs only the length mark changed (the printed consonant kept); vā 'or' is also possible in sense; the pāda has 8 syllables either way

notes: cā read as ca 'and' (minimal correction); vā 'or' would give 'failure or success'.

hindi: किन्तु असीम संकल्प वाले, ब्रह्मा की सन्तान प्रजापति इस चेतन-अचेतन जगत् के सुख और दुःख के स्रष्टा हैं।
english: Rather, Prajāpati, of boundless resolve, the offspring of Brahmā, is the creator of the pleasure and pain of this world, sentient and insentient.
notes: Continues Kāṅkāyana's view (unit 22). brahmāpatyam is a neuter noun in apposition to prajāpatiḥ ('Brahmā's offspring').

hindi: भिक्षु आत्रेय ने कहा— 'वह ठीक नहीं; क्योंकि सदा प्रजा का हित चाहने वाले प्रजापति दुर्जन की भाँति सन्तान को दुःखों से नहीं जोड़ेंगे।'
english: The mendicant (bhikṣu) Ātreya said 'That is not so': for Prajāpati, who always wishes the welfare of creatures, would not, like a wicked person, yoke (his) offspring with sorrows.

text_flags.why: the nasal before j must be the palatal ñ (yuñjyāt, optative of √yuj); ṅ before j is a misprint (Devanagari युङ्ज्याद्)

hindi: किन्तु पुरुष काल से ही उत्पन्न है और उसके रोग काल से उत्पन्न हैं; सारा जगत् काल के वश में है; काल सर्वत्र कारण है।
english: Rather, the person is born just of time, and his diseases are born of time; the whole world is under the sway of time; time is the cause everywhere.
notes: Continues the mendicant Ātreya's view (unit 24).

english: As the sages were thus disputing, Punarvasu said this: 'Do not speak so; for the truth is hard to attain by resorting to a side.'

hindi: क्योंकि जो वादों को प्रतिवादों सहित मानो वे निश्चित हों, ऐसे कहते हैं, वे तिल पेरने वाले की भाँति अपनी गति में पक्ष के अन्त तक बिल्कुल नहीं पहुँचते।
english: For those who state arguments together with counter-arguments as if they were settled never reach the end of their side, like a sesame-presser in his movement.
notes: gatau 'in going, in movement' is taken with the simile: the presser keeps moving without arriving anywhere (an interpretation of the image).

hindi: इस प्रकार वाद के संघर्ष को छोड़कर अध्यात्म का चिन्तन किया जाए; अन्धकार के समूह को दूर न किए जाने पर ज्ञेय में ज्ञान प्रवृत्त नहीं होता।
english: Having thus left aside the clash of arguments, let the inner self (adhyātma) be reflected upon; while the mass of darkness has not been shaken off, knowledge does not proceed toward the knowable.
notes: muktvā (active absolutive) with the passive anucintyatām: the agent is the sages addressed. avidhūte tamaḥskandhe is a locative absolute.

hindi: क्योंकि जिन भावों की सम्पत् मनुष्य को उत्पन्न करती है, उन्हीं की विपत् विविध व्याधियों को उत्पन्न करती है।
english: For the failure (vipad) of the very things whose excellence (sampad) would produce a man would bring forth diseases of various kinds.

hindi: तब भगवान् आत्रेय के वचन सुनकर काशिपति वामक ने फिर से भगवान् आत्रेय से कहा— 'भगवन्, सम्पत् रूपी निमित्त से उत्पन्न पुरुष की और विपत् रूपी निमित्त से उत्पन्न रोगों की अभिवृद्धि का कारण क्या है?'
english: Then, having heard the words of the venerable Ātreya, Vāmaka, lord of Kāśi, again said to the venerable Ātreya: 'Venerable one, what is the cause of growth of the person, who is born of excellence (sampad) as cause, and of the diseases, which are born of failure (vipad) as cause?'

hindi: भगवान् आत्रेय ने उससे कहा— 'एकमात्र हितकर आहार का उपयोग ही पुरुष की वृद्धि करने वाला है; किन्तु अहितकर आहार का उपयोग व्याधि का निमित्त है।'

lines_deva: तमुवाच भगवानात्रेयः हिताहारोपयोग एक एव पुरुषवृद्धिकरो भवति अहिताहारोपयोगः पुनर्व्याधिनिमित्तमिति
lines_iast: tamuvāca bhagavānātreyaḥ hitāhāropayoga eka eva puruṣavṛddhikaro bhavati ahitāhāropayogaḥ punarvyādhinimittamiti

words.gloss: in differences of measure, time, processing, place, body, doṣa, person and condition
words.gram: n. loc. pl., dvandva within tat-puruṣa

hindi: इस प्रकार बोलते हुए भगवान् आत्रेय से अग्निवेश ने कहा— 'भगवन्, यहाँ हम हितकर और अहितकर आहार-प्रकारों का अपवाद-रहित लक्षण कैसे जानें? हम देखते हैं कि हितकर कहे गए और अहितकर कहे गए आहार-प्रकार मात्रा, काल, क्रिया, भूमि, देह, दोष, पुरुष और अवस्था के भेदों में विपरीत कार्य करते हैं।'
english: To the venerable Ātreya, speaking thus, Agniveśa said: 'Venerable one, how here can we know a characteristic, free from exception, of the wholesome and unwholesome kinds of food? We observe that the kinds of food declared wholesome and those declared unwholesome act contrarily under differences of measure (mātrā), time, processing (kriyā), place (bhūmi), body, doṣa, person and condition.'

text_flags.why: the t of ahita is missing (Devanagari हिताहिआनाम्); the same line continues with hitasamākhyātānām and ahitasamākhyātānām, so the pair hita-ahita is meant

notes: Prose passage; typed as a verse in the input. puruṣāvasthā may be read as two members (person, condition) or as one ('states of the person'); antara is taken as 'difference'. upalabhāmaha = upalabhāmahe before iti (e becomes a before a vowel).
lines_deva: एवंवादिनं भगवन्तमात्रेयमग्निवेश उवाच कथमिह भगवन् हिताहिआनामाहारजातानां लक्षणमनपवादमभिजानीमहे हितसमाख्यातानामाहारजातानामहितसमाख्यातानां च मात्राकालक्रियाभूमिदेहदोषपुरुषावस्थान्तरेषु विपरीतकारित्वमुपलभामह इति
lines_iast: evaṃvādinaṃ bhagavantamātreyamagniveśa uvāca kathamiha bhagavan hitāhiānāmāhārajātānāṃ lakṣaṇamanapavādamabhijānīmahe hitasamākhyātānāmāhārajātānāmahitasamākhyātānāṃ ca mātrākālakriyābhūmidehadoṣapuruṣāvasthāntareṣu viparītakāritvamupalabhāmaha iti
